evidenceSource.method: Live files downloaded over HTTP, then rendered in Chromium with JavaScript disabled.
evidenceSource.whatIsTrustworthy: Which elements exist, their order, their CSS layout and their pixel positions.
evidenceSource.whatIsUnverified: Anything JavaScript decides from live data: which cards a real client ends up seeing, the client's real name in the greeting, and the server-loaded legal wording.
evidenceSource.note: Offsets are measured from the top of the scrolling area, which is <main>. The page does NOT scroll the window — it scrolls an inner container, so document.scrollHeight reads 900 and a naive fullPage screenshot only captures the first screen. The full-page shots here were taken at a tall viewport instead.

position.aboveOrBelowTheFold: The 1440x900 first screen shows about 848px of the scroller. The video strip starts at 764px, so only the grey strip itself peeks in at the very bottom; the title and copy are below the fold. On a 390x844 phone it starts at 920px — fully below the first screen.

b_signToAuthorizeCard.question: Is there a card or section with the text 'Sign to authorize dispute letters'?
b_signToAuthorizeCard.isItFirst: It is the FIRST card on the page and it is the hero. Only three one-line greeting <div>s sit above it, and one of those is display:none. Nothing else is visible before it.

verticalPosition.fillsTheFirstScreen: Yes. At 1440x900 it runs from 94px to 660px inside a roughly 848px-tall viewport, so it is essentially the whole first screen.

whatComesBefore: div#greeting.welcome — the headline, top of the page at 26px, reading 'Open this from a client file'
div#greeting-sub-pre.welcome-sub.precall-only — sub-line at 51px, reading 'Open this from a client file.'
div#greeting-sub.welcome-sub.funding-only — present in the markup but display:none in this state
whatComesAfter: a#fb-wins.card.fb-wins — 'Join the Fundhub wins group' at 676px
section.card.video-card — the empty welcome-video strip at 763px
b_signToAuthorizeCard.cardContents: Title, a lede ('This lets Fundhub prepare dispute letters for you. It is not a credit pull...'), the grey legal-wording slot #cpDisclosure, a 'Your legal name' text input, a 640x160 signature canvas, a Clear button, and a black button reading 'I sign to authorize Fundhub to prepare my dispute letters'.
b_signToAuthorizeCard.whyItSitsThere: public/app/client-portal.html:373-376 says it outright: 'The welcome video is ~410px. This card sat under it, so a 900px fold scan never saw "Sign to authorize". It is the one action this screen needs from an unsigned client, so it loads first.' The card was deliberately moved above the video card. Undoing that is exactly what the owner is asking for, so whoever edits it should expect a fold-position argument in the code comment and in any UI-standards check that reads it.
b_signToAuthorizeCard.complianceNote: COMPLIANCE REVIEW REQUIRED on any change to this card — it is dispute logic and consent capture (CLAUDE.md §7).
